text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.

- Banking group Merita -- which posted a 1.8 billion markka operating profit in the first half of 1997 -- should stop cutting payrolls and it start repaying its debt to the state, says Kerttu Tornqvist, socialist MP and second deputy Speaker in Parliament.

- Finnish Communist Party -- back in the party register this year -- says Leftist Alliance and the Green Party should abandon cooperation with the conservatives in the socialist-led government and join a broad red-green opposition bloc.
- State to start subsidising independent TV-programme producers to help them compete internationally.
- High wage rises in the next incomes settlements would undemine the strong economic growth, says managing director Vesa Vihriala at the Labour Institute of Economic Research.

- Sporting goods group Amer's winter season looks good as ski unit Atomic's advance sales have succeeded better than in many years before, and the unit has raised production of cross-country skis, CEO Roger Talermo says.
- Government proposal to hike tax on oil and the strong dollar will hit transport businesses hard, transporters say.
- The booming construction sector has helped furniture production, industry representatives say.
- Committee working on changes to the constitution will not propose making the President merely a figurehead, committee chairman and Green Party MP Paavo Nikula says.
- Competition between petrol stations tightens. Some service stations have cut prices, and British Station 1 chain has arrived.
- Young Finns' attitude towards soft drugs has turned more positive and many have even started to grow soft drugs, police says.
- Finland will join the European economic and monetary union (EMU) among the first countries, Prime Minister Paavo Lipponen says.
- A broad pay deal will be difficutl to achieve, Chemical Workers Union says.
